title: Sketched least squares and subspace embeddings

items.title: Rank-aware sketch-and-solve least squares
items.statement:
Input $A\in\mathbb K^{n\times p}$, $b\in\mathbb K^n$, a supplied sketch
$S\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}$, and a finite nonnegative integer SVD sweep
budget $N$, where $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Form
$C=SA$ and $c=Sb$, and call
[[alg-rank-thresholded-least-squares-by-svd]] on $(C,c)$ with threshold
$\tau=0$ and budget $N$.

If the call returns exact-arithmetic convergence with an exact SVD record,
return `success`, the exact rank $r=\operatorname{rank}(C)$, the canonical
minimum-norm vector $\widehat x=C^+c$, and the separately computed sketched
and physical residuals $\|C\widehat x-c\|_2$ and
$\|A\widehat x-b\|_2$. The exact-arithmetic solve-error certificate is
zero. If the SVD call returns `inconclusive`, return its status and supplied
partial diagnostics without claiming a minimizer. In finite precision, return
the computed candidate and the two residual reports separately; mark the rank
`unverified` unless a certified interval separates every singular-value
comparison from zero, and report a solve-error certificate only when the
solver supplies one. No finite-precision accuracy guarantee is part of this
procedure.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.5, Theorem 21
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.2

items.title: Oblivious squared-norm subspace embeddings
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $n,m\ge1$, and use
$\|x\|_2^2=\sum_i|x_i|^2$ on $\mathbb K^n$. For a fixed subspace
$U\subseteq\mathbb K^n$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, a matrix
$S\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}$ is an **$\varepsilon$-subspace embedding
for $U$** when
$$
(1-\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\le\|Sx\|_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\quad\text{for every }x\in U.
$$

For $0<\delta<1$, a distribution $\mathcal D$ on $m\times n$
matrices is an **$(\varepsilon,\delta)$ oblivious $\ell_2$ subspace
embedding for dimension $d$** if, for every fixed $d$-dimensional
subspace $U\subseteq\mathbb K^n$ chosen independently of the draw,
$$
\Pr_{S\sim\mathcal D}\{S\text{ is an }\varepsilon\text{-subspace embedding for }U\}\ge1-\delta.
$$
The subspace is fixed before sampling, but the guarantee is stated separately
for each such $U$; it does not assert that one draw preserves all
$d$-dimensional subspaces simultaneously. For a matrix $A$, an embedding
of $\operatorname{Ran}(A)$ means the property on its column space. For
least-squares residuals $Ax-b$, the relevant subspace is
$\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{Ran}(A),b)$.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.1, Definitions 1–2
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §2.1

items.title: Right preconditioner from the reduced QR factor of a sketch
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$, $S\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}$, and suppose
a reduced QR factorization of $SA$ is supplied:
$$
SA=QR,\qquad Q^*Q=I_d,
$$
where $R\in\mathbb K^{d\times d}$ is upper triangular and nonsingular.
The **sketch-QR right preconditioner** is
$$
P_S:=R^{-1}.
$$
It is undefined when no such reduced factorization with nonsingular $R$ is
available. The matrix being preconditioned is the original $A$, through
$AP_S$; $SA$ is used to construct $P_S$.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.6
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.3

items.title: Row leverage scores of a finite-dimensional subspace
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb K^n$
have dimension $d\ge1$. Choose a matrix $Q\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$
whose columns are an orthonormal basis of $U$, so $Q^*Q=I_d$. For
$0\le i<n$, define the **$i$-th row leverage score of $U$** by
$$
\ell_i(U):=\|e_i^*Q\|_2^2,
$$
where $e_i$ is the $i$-th standard coordinate vector. The following item
proves that this value is independent of the chosen orthonormal basis, so the
definition is well-defined.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.4, Definition 16
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.1

items.title: A sphere net controls a real or complex Hermitian operator norm
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$H\in\mathbb K^{d\times d}$ be Hermitian. Regard $\mathbb C^d$ as
$\mathbb R^{2d}$ for distances. A $1/4$-net $\mathcal N$ of the unit
sphere exists with $|\mathcal N|\le9^d$ over $\mathbb R$, and
$|\mathcal N|\le9^{2d}$ over $\mathbb C$. For every such net,
$$
\|H\|_2\le2\max_{v\in\mathcal N}|v^*Hv|.
$$

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.1, Lemma 5
Philippe Rigollet and Jan-Christian Hütter, High-Dimensional Statistics: Lecture Notes, Chapter 1, Lemma 1.18

items.title: Squared-norm concentration for real and normalized complex Gaussians
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $m\ge1$, and let $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be independent standard real
Gaussian scalars or independent normalized complex Gaussian scalars, with
$\mathbb E|g_j|^2=1$. For $0<t<1$,
$$
\Pr\left\{\left|\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|g_j|^2-1\right|\ge t\right\}\le2e^{-mt^2/8}.
$$

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.1, Theorem 4 and §2.2, Lemma 18
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §3.1

items.title: Leverage scores are basis-independent and sum to the dimension
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb K^n$ have dimension $d\ge1$, where
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. For any orthonormal basis matrix
$Q\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$, let $\ell_i=\|e_i^*Q\|_2^2$. Then
these values are independent of the chosen orthonormal basis, satisfy
$0\le\ell_i\le1$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\ell_i=d$, and $\ell_i=0$
exactly when the $i$-th row of $Q$ is zero.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.4
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.1

items.title: A converged exact sketch-and-solve run returns a sketch minimizer
items.statement:
Let $C=SA$ and $c=Sb$ be the sketch matrix and response in
[[alg-sketch-and-solve-least-squares]]. In exact arithmetic, if its zero-
threshold SVD call converges and supplies an exact SVD record, the returned
$\widehat x$ is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer of
$\|SAx-Sb\|_2$, and the reported rank is $\operatorname{rank}(SA)$.
No conclusion is asserted on an `inconclusive` or finite-precision
`unverified` branch.

references.title: Wen-Wei Lin, Lecture Notes of Matrix Computations, §3.2.2
David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.5

items.title: An embedded QR right preconditioner has controlled singular values
items.statement:
Let $n,m,d\ge1$ with $n,m\ge d$, let $A\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$ have full column rank, and let
$0<\varepsilon<1$, and suppose the particular matrix $S$ is an
$\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{Ran}(A)$. A reduced
QR factorization $SA=QR$ exists and has nonsingular $R$, so the
preconditioner $P_S=R^{-1}$ of
[[def-sketch-qr-right-preconditioner]] is defined. Its right-preconditioned
matrix satisfies
$$
\frac1{\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}}\le\sigma_{\min}(AP_S)\le\sigma_{\max}(AP_S)\le\frac1{\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}},\qquad \kappa_2(AP_S):=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(AP_S)}{\sigma_{\min}(AP_S)}\le\sqrt{\frac{1+\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}}.
$$

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.6
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.3

items.title: With-replacement leverage-score row sampling and rescaling
items.statement:
Input an orthonormal basis matrix $Q\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$ with
$d\ge1$, a sample count $m\ge1$, a parameter $0<\beta\le1$, and a
probability vector $\pi=(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{n-1})$ satisfying
$\pi_i\ge\beta\ell_i(U)/d$, where $U=\operatorname{Ran}(Q)$ and
$\ell_i(U)$ is from [[def-subspace-leverage-scores]]. If the input checks
fail, return `invalid-input`. Otherwise draw indices $J_1,\ldots,J_m$
independently with replacement from $\pi$. Form $S\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}$
by setting row $j$ to $e_{J_j}^*/\sqrt{m\pi_{J_j}}$, and return `success`,
the selected indices, and $S$.

Because $\beta>0$, $\pi_i=0$ implies $\ell_i(U)=0$; such a row is
never sampled, so the scaling never divides by zero. One canonical choice is
$\pi_i=\ell_i(U)/d$, which sets every zero-leverage row's probability to
zero. Other admissible distributions may assign positive probability to a
zero-leverage row, but that choice wastes samples. Repeated indices are
allowed and are distinct rows of $S$.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.4, Definition 16
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.2

items.title: Gaussian sketches embed a fixed subspace at the additive dimension rate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $1\le d\le n$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$U\subseteq\mathbb K^n$ be a fixed $d$-dimensional subspace. Let
$G\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}$ have iid standard real Gaussian entries when
$\mathbb K=\mathbb R$, or iid normalized complex Gaussian entries with
$\mathbb E|g|^2=1$ when $\mathbb K=\mathbb C$. Put $S=G/\sqrt m$.
For $0<\varepsilon,\delta<1$, if
$$
m\ge192\varepsilon^{-2}\bigl(d+\log(1/\delta)\bigr),
$$
then with probability at least $1-\delta$, $S$ is an
$\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $U$. Thus this Gaussian distribution
is an $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ oblivious $\ell_2$ subspace embedding for
dimension $d$.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.1, Theorem 6
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §3.1

items.title: Embedding span(A,b) gives the sketch-and-solve residual factor
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb K^{n\times p}$, $b\in\mathbb K^n$, and
$0<\varepsilon<1$. Suppose the particular sketch $S$ used in
[[alg-sketch-and-solve-least-squares]] is an $\varepsilon$-subspace
embedding for
$U=\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{Ran}(A),\{b\})$. If that algorithm
returns an exact-arithmetic converged vector $\widehat x$, then
$$
\|A\widehat x-b\|_2^2\le\frac{1+\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}\min_{x\in\mathbb K^p}\|Ax-b\|_2^2.
$$
Embedding $\operatorname{Ran}(A)$ alone is not a hypothesis for this
conclusion.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.5, Theorem 21
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.2

items.title: Leverage-score row sampling embeds the column space
items.statement:
Let $Q\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$, $d\ge1$, have orthonormal columns,
and let $\ell_i=\|e_i^*Q\|_2^2$. Let $\pi$ be a probability vector
with $\pi_i\ge\beta\ell_i/d$ for $0<\beta\le1$, and draw $S$ by
[[alg-leverage-score-row-sampling-sketch]] with replacement. For
$0<\varepsilon,\delta<1$, if
$$
m\ge\frac{8d}{\beta\varepsilon^2}\log\left(\frac{2d}{\delta}\right),
$$
then with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$$
\|Q^*S^*SQ-I_d\|_2\le\varepsilon.
$$
Equivalently, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for
$\operatorname{Ran}(Q)$. In the usual confidence range
$0<\delta\le1/2$, the simpler sufficient condition
$$
m\ge\frac{16d}{\beta\varepsilon^2}\log\left(\frac d\delta\right)
$$
follows. For a matrix $A$ of rank $d$, any orthonormal basis $Q$ of
$\operatorname{Ran}(A)$ gives the corresponding embedding guarantee on
$\operatorname{Ran}(A)$.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.4, Theorem 17
David Woodruff, 15-859T Lecture 4.2, Leverage Score Sampling gives a Subspace Embedding, Claims 2–3
Joel A. Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, §6.6

title: Sketched least squares and subspace embeddings — Examples

items.title: Embedding Ran(A) alone does not control the sketch-and-solve residual
items.statement:
False claim: If $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for
$\operatorname{Ran}(A)$, then every exact sketch least-squares minimizer
$\widehat x$ satisfies
$$
\|A\widehat x-b\|_2^2\le\frac{1+\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}\min_x\|Ax-b\|_2^2.
$$

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.5, Theorem 21
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.2

items.title: Zero leverage rows and a maximally coherent one-dimensional design
items.statement:
Take $Q=e_1=(1,0,0)^T\in\mathbb R^{3\times1}$. Compute its leverage
scores and compare one exact leverage-proportional sample with one uniform
row sample. Define the coherence here by
$\mu(U)=(n/d)\max_i\ell_i(U)$.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.4
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.1

items.title: An exact two-row sketch for a three-row regression problem
items.statement:
Let $A=(1,1,1)^T$, $b=e_1$, and let $S\in\mathbb R^{2\times3}$
have rows $q_1^T=(1,1,1)/\sqrt3$ and
$q_2^T=(2,-1,-1)/\sqrt6$. Compute the original and sketched least-squares
minimizers and residuals.

references.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra, §2.5, Theorem 21
Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data, §4.2
